A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Point Prompting work. All 20 pages of each version, including equations, figures, tables, references, and appendices, support comparison. Relocated material and renumbered tables can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original tracking experiments on TAP-Vid DAVIS, Kinetics, and Kubric, with quantitative comparisons, ablations, and qualitative examples.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds results for a CoTracker trained using generator-produced trajectories.

M1.justification: v2 adds a teacher–student procedure: generate trajectory pseudo-labels with the Wan2.1-1.3B-based method, train CoTracker from scratch, and perform tracking through the trained network. v1 mentioned distillation only as a possible future extension. This introduces a substantial training and inference branch; the original point-prompting pipeline remains unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions cover point tracking on TAP-Vid DAVIS, Kinetics, and Kubric. The distillation experiment reuses Kinetics for training and DAVIS for evaluation without introducing a new represented domain or task. Its additional samples and training role affect the experimental protocol.

E2.justification: New Table 5 directly compares the Wan2.1-1.3B teacher with a distilled CoTracker trained from scratch. This adds a teacher–student comparison, distinct from the existing supervised CoTracker3 baseline. Comparator membership in the retained DAVIS/Kinetics and Kubric benchmark tables is unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 introduces training on trajectories generated from 1,000 unlabeled TAP-Vid Kinetics videos, followed by a DAVIS teacher–student evaluation. The existing benchmark subsets, first-query sampling, metrics, resolutions, and diffusion settings remain unchanged. Detailed student training and evaluation settings are not supplied.

E4.justification: The new distillation study tests whether generated trajectories provide useful supervision for a separate tracker, using teacher–student accuracy comparisons as evidence. Existing component, resolution, backbone, guidance, marker-color, and tracker ablations are unchanged. The failure examples move into the main text without new cases.

E5.justification: Neither version reports tracking-result seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The new distillation table likewise reports point estimates only.

E6.justification: All nine original tables retain their numerical entries. New Table 5 reports teacher AJ/positional accuracy/OA of 38.78/54.75/85.00 and distilled CoTracker results of 37.17/53.12/84.24. These are additional results; the settings explaining the teacher's difference from its unchanged Table 2 AJ of 44.58 are unspecified, so no same-setting decline is established.

T1.justification: Equations 1–8, the diffusion and inpainting definitions, and the score-function reasoning for counterfactual guidance remain unchanged. The distillation addition introduces no formal objective, theorem, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction add a contribution claiming that generator-produced trajectories can train a fast tracker with comparable performance. v1 presented distillation as a possible efficiency remedy. The principal claims about zero-shot tracking, occlusion handling, and counterfactual prompting remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the student–teacher comparison as evidence that temporal reasoning capabilities can transfer into an efficient tracking network. Existing interpretations of occlusion handling, generation quality, and synthetic-video failures remain unchanged. The relocated limitations text still describes distillation prospectively despite the new experiment.

D1.justification: The added study identifies the teacher, student architecture, pseudo-label source, 1,000-video training sample, and from-scratch initialization. It does not provide an optimizer, training schedule, or measured student runtime. The original implementation appendix is retained unchanged as Appendix B, and access information is unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and substantive positioning remain unchanged. The added Karaev et al. 2024d reference duplicates the CoTracker work already cited as 2024c. The connection between distillation and Stojanov et al. was already stated in v1.

P1.justification: v2 adds an abstract sentence, contribution bullet, and distillation discussion. It moves Limitations from Appendix A to Section 6 and adjusts subsequent section and appendix labels. Most existing prose is retained verbatim.

P2.justification: v2 adds the small distillation Table 5, relocates Figure 7 from the appendix into the main text, and redistributes Figure 6 and existing tables across pages. Existing figures retain their content, and the original appendix tables are renumbered without numerical changes.

improvement.justification: v1 identified expensive per-point generation and suggested distillation; v2 provides a concrete demonstration, with student AJ of 37.17 versus its teacher's 38.78 in Table 5. This adds useful evidence that generated trajectories can supervise a tracker, while moving limitations into the main text improves their visibility. The gain is limited by missing speed measurements and training details, unexplained differences between teacher results across tables, and retained language describing distillation as hypothetical.
